title: How the order notification text is built (Python)
context:
## Starting point

The test `test_orders.py` calls `build_order_notification` with an order of **2 products** and the coupon `WELCOME`.

We want to see, with real values, where each part of the text comes from: the subtotal, the coupon discount, the amount formatting and the final `body`.

steps.title: Entry: the order arrives
steps.comment: `build_order_notification` receives the whole order. Look at `coupon_code`: it decides whether "you saved" shows up later.

highlights.note: the whole notification is built here

steps.title: Subtotal per line
steps.comment: Each item becomes a line with `total = unit_price × quantity`. The subtotal does **not** include the discount yet.

steps.title: Coupon discount
steps.comment: The rate comes from the `DISCOUNTS` table. An unknown (or missing) coupon gives a rate of `0`.

steps.anchorText: discount_text = f" (you saved {format_amount(discount)})" if discount > 0 else ""
steps.title: Amount formatted
steps.comment: The total after the discount, as text.

steps.title: The text is assembled
steps.comment: The final `body` joins the customer name, the number of lines, the amount and the discount text.
